Deux façons de compter, expliquées pas à: Two ways of counting, explained step by step. Read and listen first; the exercises come after.
(일, 이, 삼…) servent notamment aux prix, a: numbers (일, 이, 삼…) are used in particular for prices, dates and minutes. The
(하나, 둘, 셋…) servent notamment à compter: numbers (하나, 둘, 셋…) are used in particular to count objects, give your age with 살 and tell the hour.
Un chiffre est un signe de 0 à 9. Un nom: A digit is a sign from 0 to 9. A number can contain several digits: 25 is read 이십오 in the Sino-Korean system and 스물다섯 in the native system.
Pour zéro, retiens 영 dans les nombres et: For zero, remember 영 in numbers and 공 in phone numbers. There is no zero in the native series shown here.
Devant un compteur, 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세: Before a counter, 하나 → 한, 둘 → 두, 셋 → 세, 넷 → 네 and 스물 → 스무. So: 한 개 (one object), 세 명 (three people), 스무 살 (20 years old). At 21: 스물한 살.
= c’est. → « Il est 15 h 20. » Une seule: = it is. → “It’s 3:20 pm.” A single sentence uses both systems!
